author: Stefan84
quote:
A fantastic remake of the original NES-classic! 
The visuals and animations are so well done, and it has a lot of great humor. The exaggerated expressions of the characters are hilarious, I really made me laugh.

It's too bad it didn't really sell that well, so we probably won't see a game like this from Nintendo again.. Some probably took a look at the box-art and took the game for a generic, family-friendly boxing sim with cartoonish visuals.

But it's not a boxing sim at all, it's an arcade-style action game, where you have to memorize patterns and dodge in order to beat the, increasingly, very challenging opponents. Some of the later boxers are really tough, with quick combos. I really struggled with many of them!

Nintendo at their best, fantastic game!

author: Stefan84
quote:
I can understand all the backlash this game has gotten, because the story is unfortunately pretty abysmal. Samus went from an independent, badass space bounty-hunter, to an insecure little girl who has to let someone else decide if or when she can use her powers - instead of finding them throughout the world when solving puzzles etc. There are also lenghty, un-skippable cutscenes in the game, some longer than 10-15 minutes.

So what are the redeeming qualities of this game you might ask..? For me it's the action gameplay, as well as some of the boss fights. They're excellent for the most part. I also quite like to explore the world with it's great visuals. Other than the story, this is classic Metroid. So there's definitely a great game hiding in here.

author: Stefan84
quote:
Although a pretty great game overall, it does not hold the quality I expect from a 3D Mario game. It simply feels like a generic "been there, done that" game. Coming off of the masterful Mario Galaxy games, I feel Nintendo had ran out of ideas here, and just created an experience that feels a bit stale.

It feels like it was directed at smaller children a bit too much, so playing this as an adult fan of the 3D Mario games felt quite underwhelming.

I am still giving it an 8, because the gameplay is still solid Mario platforming. It feels great to control, some of the levels are memorable - although most are not unfortunately.

author: Stefan84
quote: This game is a complete scam! It’s a boyfriend simulator disguised as a GTA game, making it closer to Sims 5 than anything else.. Also, get used to frequently seeing fps-dips into the low 20’s during gameplay - for a AAA game in 2026, with near 10 years development time.

author: Stefan84
quote: The game is simply awful, as most gamers know by now. Stay away from it and and keep you sanity.

author: Stefan84
quote:
I finished this game after a nearly 40-hour playthrough - the Legendary Edition on Ps5 that is, and I had a blast throughout most of the experience.

I especially liked how EDI is now available to select as a team-mate for missions, since she has taken form as a female android. She is a really well-written and interesting character, and develops her personality throughout the game's story.

I also don't really see the problem with the game's ending(s), as I found them to be quite fitting as a conclusion to the trilogy. It is truly thought-provoking, and makes you really think about how you want it all to end. None of the 4 available endings are without major consequenses for something or someone you care about, so picking the right one isn't actually that straightforward, even though one of them probably is preferable to most players, and probably considered the "best/correct" choice to end the story.

This trilogy has one of the best written, and most thought-provoking stories I've ever encountered in video games - simply masterful story-telling on display here. (except for a couple of examples of forced incluisivity in ME3) It makes you genuinely care about your team-mates, and the people you meet along the way, to the extend that you want to make the "right" decisions as you progress.

This one definitely leans most towards the action/shooter genre of the three games, but there are lots of room for role-play here as well, with decision-making that changes how the story progresses. The combat also feels the best in the series overall, with enhanced emphasis on Shepards abilities during action encounters.

A few things I didn't like is how the game doesn't really tell you if the missions you are selecting are part of the base-game story, or part of the DLC that came later, so I ended up finishing DLC-missions pretty early in the game, but I would've liked to play through the main story first. The game is not very clear on that - so some sort of warning would be nice.

Also during combat, Shepard seems to automatically just stick to any surface for cover during a shoot-out, and this isn't always ideal when you are trying to run from enemies if they overwhelm you. If you haven't picked a spot behing cover far enough from multiple enemies, you actually risk getting stun-locked when trying to run and find cover in a more ideal position, as Shephard will just stick to the nearest wall or crate available.

These are minor complaints in an otherwise fantastic experience, and I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game.

author: Stefan84
quote:
This game has fallen far away from whay made the original trilogy good. There are several new, highly unlikable characters, and the story has suffered immensely for it.
I don't recommend!

author: Stefan84
quote: Without mentioning the huge elephant in the room, I'll simply say don't waste your time or money on this garbage - it's made for anyone who's not a real gamer.

author: Stefan84
quote:
I missed these games during their initial launch as I wasn't into RPG's at the time, but having instead played them all recently in this updated release, means I got to enjoy the best possible version of them, with 4K resolution in 60fps - so needless to say, I have no regrets!

There are also general updates to the visuals as well as gameplay, which Mass Effect 1 benefits greatly from, as that one had aged rather poorly compared to the other two.

A great package overall, with 90+ hours of gameplay!

Ps: Also refreshing to se "male" "female" during character creation, instead of "body type" 1, 2, 3, 4 etc.. This is how great gaming used to be before everything went woke.

author: Stefan84
quote:
A fantastic RPG where most of your decisions have a real impact on the people, as well as the world around you.
You meet a lot of interesting characters along this 30+ hour journey, and many of them eventually become crewmates on your spaceship. It's genuinely intriguing to get to know most characters and develop a deeper connection with them as you play and the story unfolds.

The gameplay also feels quite satisfying, with lots of shooting and action during missions. And you can choose from several weapons - in each weapon class, which you can also level up.
I particularly liked the final mission in the game, where you have to make several real-time decisions on the go, and there are potentially major consequences following your actions.

One thing I didn't particularly like, is how simplistic the leveling system is. It unfortunately isn't very deep and interesting. Instead of having a skill tree, where you level up certain character traits - like "charisma" for example, you level up a trait of your choosing by making real-time decisions during some cutscenes, called paragon or renegade.

This would actually be interesting and fine, if the game was a little clearer as to the consequences of not sticking to just one type of decision-making during each playthrough. I missed out on several key dialogue options, which you are rewarded with for sticking to only one of the two options, which again negatively affected my relationship with a companion - she went sour on me for the rest of the playtrough, and I couldn't do anything about it.

I like the leveling system in Fallout 4, for instance, a lot more due to it being a lot deeper and it's immediately clear that having a high level of "charisma" means you'll pass higher-level speech checks more easily.

What I Did really like about the leveling system however, is that there's no grinding here. Instead of gaining experience from defeating enemies and bosses etc, you level up after each mission instead, and can distribute the level points you get freely over the few skills available.

Aside from this however, the game has a deep, intriguing story, excellent voice performances, great writing, as well as entertaining action gameplay.
I was pretty much hooked until the very end.

author: Stefan84
quote:
Another fun Mario platformer in the "new" series, this time for the 3DS, and you get exactly what you expect from a game like this.
The levels are fun, the controls precise, and with some cool power-ups. 

Being the 3rd game in the series, and not really offering anything new, it probably had become a bit stale at that point. But a pretty great game nonetheless.

author: Stefan84
quote:
Nintendo's introduction to the HD-era - better late than never, and it was pretty exciting seeing a Super Mario game in high definition for the first time, even though it almost just looks like the Wii version with a fresh coat of paint.

It doesn't really do anything new in the "new" series, but rather builds upon the existing games with a few power-ups and fun levels.

author: Stefan84
quote:
Don't be turned off by the title and box-art of this game, as it's a surprisingly deep and challenging little strategy-game.

Your character is a young boy who has found a mysterious crown which gives him the power to charm people and make them follow orders. You command your minion followers to fight enemies - Pikmin-style, and expand your kingdom, as well as make your population grow and be happy.

It's a really addicting gameplay-loop, and it's lots of fun figuring out the best strategy, for exploration as well as enemy encounters.

There are a few negatives however, which Imo, keeps the game from true greatness. The camera can sometimes be a bit problematic when trying to navigate the terrain with lots of minions, and there's also no map, which just makes it really hard to figure out where to go as the world opens up and gets bigger.
This ended up being my biggest gripe with it, as the experience became quite frustrating without a map.

But overall, a lengthy, fun strategy-game with lots of charm!

author: Stefan84
quote:
The start of the "new" Super Mario series, and it was really great fun playing a Mario platformer with this level of creativity on a handheld.

It is probably my least favorite in the series, since the others do what this game does a lot better, but It's definitely a worthy playthrough still if you find it for a decent price.

author: Stefan84
quote:
My personal favorite of the "new" Super Mario series, as this is the one I had the most fun with, considering I've played them all.
You really can't go wrong with any one of them if you're looking for some simple, fun, platforming delight.

I guess I really liked some of the worlds in this one the most, as well as some of the power-ups.
An excellent platformer in the Mario universe, where you can play couch co-op with family and friends!

author: Stefan84
quote:
This game is just.. weird! It's hard to explain the experience I had with it. Most of the time, I guess it plays out like an action/adventure game, but it's also kind of a mini-game compilation.
The characters and story are somewhat interesting, and made me want to see it through to the end. The visuals are also pretty nice, with some great texture-work.

But the combat leaves a bit to be desired, as you mostly just use the pointer controls to pick up objects and throw them at enemies. Which becomes a bit repetetive after a while. You can also pick up enemies themselves to throw them around, or at other foes. It's fun for the first few battles, but I wish there were deeper mechanics introduced as the game goes on.

Overall a pretty fun, but mostly forgettable adventure on the Wii.
game_title: Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers

author: Stefan84
quote:
An okay follow-up to the first game, but nothing really groundbreaking to set it apart from the first experience.
The motion controls also felt less responsive to me in this one, so I just stuck with the pro controller.

But the game was interesting enough for me to see it all the way through, so a pretty fun experience overall - with even more impressive visuals than the first.

A pretty short, but definitely decent FPS.

author: Stefan84
quote:
A pretty solid FPS-experience overall. As far as the genre goes, it's a bit generic and nothing we haven't seen before, but for some reason I actually really liked it.

It has some great visuals for it's time, and the controls are spot on - some great use of the pointer controls here, making aiming seamless.
The story and overall plot is nothing to write home about, but the action is constant, and the shooting feels great for the most part.

At the time, there wasn't really much for Wii owners to compare this experience to, so we took what we could get. 
But I'd say it's an objectively fun game overall, if you're into the FPS-genre.

author: Stefan84
quote:
Pretty simple and easy? Certainly. But a really fun experience nonetheless. I really like the world design, and the platforming in these bite-sized levels feels great. Mario feels great to control as usual with these games, with some new as well as returning power-ups. 
And after the end credits, you get to try out some more challenging levels.

author: Stefan84
quote:
The problem with this game, is that I finished BOTW three times before going into this, and had gotten my fill of it.
This felt like starting the exact same game all over again, only a less fun version of it. Solving shrine-puzzles just like before, finding Korok seeds to expand you inventory slots, weapons breaking after a few hits, visiting the same locations as the previous game.. I got so bored with it I quit about half-way through, and have little interest in ever picking it back up.

If you somehow missed BOTW , and this is your first experience, I'm sure it is a great game, and you'll probably get the feeling I had playing the former for the first time.

But as someone who explored everything the first game had to offer over hundreds of hours, this experience is mediocre at best. I really hope Nintendo comes up with something new for the next installment in the series, as I've personally had my fill with these cell-shaded, open-world experiments.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition

author: Stefan84
quote:
A much-needed change to a gaming formula that perhaps had become a bit stale.
This was pretty revolutionary game design, as it is the first open-world game that felt truly "open", as in go anywhere you like right at the beginning.

You want to go right for the final boss? Once you leave the Great plateu you can absolutely do that if you're crazy enough.

I just was in awe the first time playing it, and couldn't put the game down! You can explore anywhere you want, climb any surface, visit any town/village and tackle any boss in any order you want. There are also tons of interesting characters with lost of side-quests you meet along your journey.
No two player had the exact same experience with it, it was simply a masterpiece in game design.
The best game in the entire franchise for me, and Nintendo at it's best!
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

author: Stefan84
quote:
Just coming off of Twilight Princess, which I really loved, into this, I was a bit disappointed at the linear design and hand-holding in comparison. 

But during my second playthrough of it a few years later, I came to appreciate it a lot more, and now think of it as a fantastic addition to the franchise overall.

The story and atmosphere is great, and you also meet some fun, quirky characters along the way that are pretty interesting.
And it has perhaps the best final boss fight in the entire franchise, I was genuinely impressed.

I'm probably also one of the few who actually liked the motion controls, and thought they added a lot to the overall experience. They worked well for the most part Imo.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD

author: Stefan84
quote:
A really fun, lenghty adventure starring two of the most beloved protagonists in gaming.
I particularly liked the combat mechanics in Luigi's dreamworld, it keeps the game interesting throughout.

author: Stefan84
quote:
A really fun, ableit somewhat shallow adventure game with pretty good visuals for it's time.
A cool, unique mechanic in the game is making weapons out of small items you find throughout the worlds you explore, like bottlecaps, wooden sticks, razor's, pencils etc.
I was actually surprised at how much fun it is.

author: Stefan84
quote:
Perhaps one of the biggest atrocities made in video game history. A game so bad it single-handedly shut down the game-studio responsible for it.

This proves that the "modern audience" doesn't really exist, and real gamers don't want games with modern politics forced into them, but with a genuinely good story, backed up with great gameplay and visuals.

author: Stefan84
quote:
I didn’t get to play this game until several years after the Gamecube was even discontinued, as I never owned the system as a kid.

But after being introdused to it by a Youtuber in 2011, I found a cheap copy at a local Gamestop, and picked it up.
The game admittedly is quite short, but when you’re having fun most of those few hours, that’s not necessarily a negative thing. 

It was such a unique and fun experience, with great visuals and lighting effects - I particularly love how the flashlight Luigi carries with him casts shadows in the environment in a realistic way when he uses it, very impressive for a GCN launch title.

author: Stefan84
quote:
A fantastic action/adventure game, that really shows Lara's more human side if you will.  
She starts out as a young inexperienced treasure hunter with a team of fellow explorers, but after their ship gets wrecked on an hostile island, she's left to fend for herself, and slowly but surely has to learn to survive, and eventually becomes a competent action heroine who knows how to handle herself.

Gone is the macho, obnoxious - and Imo, masculine Lara Croft of older titles - not to mention the movie adaptations starring Angelina Jolie! This game shows of a more feminine version of her, with real human fears and insecurities, which is a lot more believable.

The gameplay is also top-notch, and has good pacing, controls and action sequences including shooting mechanics. I also liked exploring the countless tombs and solving the puzzles.

As expected from an modern-day action game, there are quite a few quick-time events, but in my opinion they're done reasonably well here.

author: Stefan84
quote:
One of my favorite games of all time, and in my opinion - the greatest platformer/adventure game that's ever been created, and the best game on the N64 - period!

It's hard for me to fathom the level of orginality and creativity for a game of this age, and it still holds up really well even today. I have probably played through it 10-15 times over the years since I was a kid, and it never really gets old.

Mario 64, although groundbreaking when it came out, gets much of the spotlight as a 3D-platformer, but this game offers so much more creativity and has aged a lot better, so I don't think it really gets the recognition it deserves for how amazing of an experience it is.

author: Stefan84
quote:
I'd seen a lot of praise for this game and decided to give it a try, since I really like 3D-platformers. 
But too me, this genre has felt a bit stale ever since the amazing Mario Galaxy games, (yes even counting Mario Odyssey) so I didn't think it would be that special.

But oh boy was I wrong - it didn't take long for me to get lost in this amazing experience. The level of creativity in this game is simply astonishing! It rivals, and often even exceeds that of Mario Galaxy! And that is the highest compliment I can give a platformer, since it's one of my favorite games of all time. I actually felt like I was playing the sequel we never got from Nintendo, but with actual modern visuals. To me, this is a spiritual successor to Mario Galaxy 2.

While playing, I just sat there shaking my head and grinning at the same time, in awe of the creativity throughout the entire experience. Every level and world has something new to offer, with new power-ups, ways to manipulate the environment, and not to mention the music, so it never gets repetitive.
This is the most genuine video game experience that's been released in a long time - no cut-scenes, no boring walk-and-talk sequences, no excessive tutorials, just a really entertaining time from start to finish.

I also have to mention the controls - they're virtually perfect! Astro Bot feels so good and responsive to control in every way he moves, so it makes the gameplay that much more fluid and fun. In some later challenging levels I died A LOT, but it was always down to me, as I timed my jumps or other movements incorrectly.
The motion controls in this game is also expertly implemented, and proves they're far from dead - when used in really creative ways like in this game, and not just gimmicky. They actually do add a lot to the overall gameplay and fun-factor.

It is also perhaps the most visually impressive game I've ever played, not just counting the artstyle, but also on a technical level - it simply looks amazing in every way! It has some seriously catchty tunes as well, which got stuck in my head for days after playing.

This game made a grown man like me feel like I did when I played Banjo Kazooie for the first time as a kid - I cannot recommend it enough! The only downside is, Sony set the bar too high with this one, so I'll probably be an old man the next time I experience anything close to this masterpiece.

author: Stefan84
quote:
This was one of my first Pc-gaming experiences as a kid, and I was instantly addicted.
I have played it for probably well over a thousand hours, and still play occasionally to this day - it never gets old. It is just too much fun to play around with the Map editor, and create your own worlds for the heroes to conquer. One of my favorite games of all time for sure!
game_title: Heroes of Might and Magic III Complete

author: Stefan84
quote:
I just finished the game today with north of 15 hours of total playtime, and it was a really unique experience.
It has a gripping and quite touching story, as well as interesting gameplay and combat mechanics.

And.perhaps the best part: there was no modern "message" to be found, I didn’t find any woke nonsense during my playthrough, which is unusual these days.
It is simply just a fun and interesting game focusing on just that - being entertaining. Props to Capcom!

author: Stefan84
quote:
This was my first experience with the Metroid universe, and I was simply drawn into it's amazing world almost instantly!
What really clicked with me was the ingenious level design, and how puzzles are integrated into the world in such an interesting way. The pacing is near perfect, the way you slowly discover new suit and weapon upgrades, and use them to progress through earlier non-reachable areas is so masterfully planned out. I also particularly loved how they implemented Samus' ship into some of the puzzles, as well as used it for fast travel between areas. There's a bit less back-tracking in this one, compared to Prime 1 & 2. I have since played most of the games in the Metroid franchise - both 3D and 2D, and it's one of my favorites of all time, and this game in particular holds a special place in my heart. I have finished it several times over the years!

author: Stefan84
quote:
I think the game starts off very interesting, and as the story enfolded, it made me stick with it to the end.
But I don't know, there's just something about it, there are too many twists and turns in the story near the ending, it all gets very confusing and I got burned out on it - almost like the story got lost in translation or something.
As an action/adventure game, there are many others which do what this game does much better Imo.
I also didn't feel compelled to explore the world outside of the linear story progression, it simply wasn't that interesting too me. +++Positives: The combat was pretty fun however, the visuals impressive, and a certain likeable character you meet mid-game which joins your journey.
Overall a pretty good, but severely over-hyped game, that didn't really click with me unfortunately.

author: Stefan84
quote:
This was my introduction to the Zelda universe, and It made me instantly love the franchise - as well as the action/adventure genre in general.
Before getting a Wii and this game, I had been very casually into video games for years, but from the videos I saw and all the hype I heard from Zelda fans, this looked very interesting to me. And I'm really glad I played it, as it became one of my favorite Zelda's, as well as games of all time!
This took many of OoT's ideas and perfected them. It was engaging from the start, and I have finished it several times.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess

author: Stefan84
quote:
I didn't play this game when it came out for the N64, as I was just casually into video games at that time, so my review is based on the quality of this game as a "modern" title - not based on nostalgia.
I can see why this game is as hyped up as it is, as I can imagine it was very revolutionary for it's time, and I think it's an overall great experience - albeit dated, even today.
But for someone who didn't get to play it until the remake on the 3DS, most of it's mechanics have not aged well, and newer games in the franchise have definitely done much better in the action/adventure universe.
But as stated earlier, it is overall a great game even today, and it is mostly a fun experience, although with some frustration moments.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D

author: Stefan84
quote:
A fantastic follow-up to one of my favorite games of all time! I slightly prefer the first one, probably because it was so revolutionary, and felt so new.
But the inclusion of Yoshi as well as many new innovative stages, makes this game as much of a must play as the first one!

author: Stefan84
quote:
What a treasure this masterpiece is! I remember getting a Wii and this game in 2011, after a long time of not being interested in video games, and just pursuing other interests and hobbies.
What an almost magical moment it was playing this game, it made an adult man like me feel like the kid I was, getting my Nes for Christmas in the early 90's.
The platforming is absolutely superb, the music is exhilarating, and the pacing is simply perfect. One of the best games Nintendo has ever made!

author: Stefan84
quote:
This must seriously be the most overrated game in existence! It does not feel like a video game, but a boring interactive movie, where the player barely does any actual playing at all.
The amount of cut-scenes, walk-and-talk sequences, as well as quick-time events made this game nearly unplayable for me.
The final nail in the coffin was the extremely out-of-place Angrboda story, which doesn't seem to fit in the general narrative at all, it just seems shoehorned in for some reason.. (I wonder why) Isn't this game supposed to be based on Norse Mythology..?
There's probably a good game hidden in there somewhere, but it's completely overshadowed by the flaws I just mentioned, so I won't even bother mentioning the somewhat good aspects.

author: Stefan84
quote:
I just finished this game today after spending about 70 hours playing 
it - almost non stop!
I'm usually not into turn-based combat in RPG's, and prefer action styles, but this game really made me a believer. This has to be one of the most engaging combat-systems in video game history! Kind of blending the best of both worlds, I really loved the 
parry/counter-attack mechanic, and once you get the hang of it, it's truly addictive.
The combat and several of the game's bosses remind me of Elden Ring - another game I love!
I also have to commend the music in this game, so many memorable scores that stuck in my head, and with different tunes for each combat encounter, amazing stuff!
I played the game for several hours each day, and when I didn't play it, I was still thinking about it.
Highly recommended!

author: Stefan84
quote:
I am a huge fan of the Metroid Prime games, but hadn't really gotten that much into the 2D-series, so I went into this thinking I might like it a little bit, but it probably won't be anything special.

But man was I wrong, I was pretty much hooked within the first hour, and struggled to put it down until the very finish!

The exploration, puzzle-solving, sense of isolation and atmoshere is like no other. The developers did a fantastic job nailing the Metroid-experience!

The game is also pretty challenging, with several of the bosses making me really break a sweat. This is definitely one of my favorite Nintendo-games in recent years!

author: Stefan84
quote:
Three of my favorite games of all time, in a single package, with the first two greatly enhanced with Wii pointer controls, making shooting, puzzle-solving, and looking around in general that much better.

Prime 3 is definitely my favorite, but all 3 are timeless classics which I still occasionally play to this day.

author: Stefan84
quote:
A really great game, with lots of different quirky weapons to play around with. It has lots of action and fun exploration, and really held my interest from start to finish.
I really liked the one on Ps4, so I was looking forward to this as well, and it did not disappoint.

It is slightly on the easy side on nomal mode, so if you're a veteran, you probably should try out a harder difficulty for an enhanced challenge.

author: Stefan84
quote:
What a fantastic experience this masterpiece is! Games like this only show up once every 5-10 years, and it stays in your mind for a long time after you've finished it.

The world is simply enthralling, filled with secrets to uncover. I have probably played through it upwards of 10 times now, experimenting with different builds. And I still find content I missed in earlier playthroughs.

One of my top 10 favorite games of all time fo sure!

author: Stefan84
quote:
I was hoping to experience a new Metroid Prime game in all it’s greatness - like past entries, but instead got a mixed bag of modern slop obviously meant to appeal to anyone who’s not a real fan of the original trilogy.
And yes it's true, you actually have to pay an extra $30 for an Amiibo if you want to have music while riding your bike in the desert area, and you'll be driving there A LOT, so get ready for some tedious, silent hours.

If this indeed is Nintendo’s way of revitalizing the Prime series, it should‘ve just been left in the desert..
